item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Mostly no. Tshisekedi made one notable women’s-inclusion move in 2024 by appointing the country’s first female prime minister, and he backed at least one local peace arrangement in an excluded/conflict-affected area. But the broader 2024 record is dominated by repression of opposition, activists, journalists, and protesters, plus unequal treatment in conflict zones and weak protection for vulnerable groups.

**Accepted Claims**

- **DR Congo names first female prime minister amid escalating violence** | Reuters | 2024-04-01 | [URL](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/dr-congo-president-appoints-countrys-first-female-prime-minister-2024-04-01/)  
  Tshisekedi appointed Judith Suminwa Tuluka as DRC’s first female prime minister. This is the clearest positive evidence for women’s political equality in 2024, though it is symbolic and does not by itself show broader equality reforms.  
  IDs: `4B.7` `4B.5`

- **Les Téké et les Yaka s’engagent à mettre fin aux hostilités dans l’ouest de la Rdc** | Présidence RDC | 2024-04-06 | [URL](https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/les_teke_et_les_yaka_sengagent_a_mettre_fin_aux_hostilites_dans_louest_de_la_rdc)  
  Tshisekedi presided over a local peace agreement in western DRC where Téké and Yaka representatives committed to dialogue, mediation, and arbitration. This is limited positive evidence that he sometimes supported equal treatment and de-escalation for communities in conflict-affected, politically marginalized areas.  
  IDs: `4B.7` `4B.4`

- **DR Congo: Second Term Should Focus on Rights** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-03-06 | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/06/dr-congo-second-term-should-focus-rights)  
  HRW said Tshisekedi’s first term had been marked by intolerance for dissent and narrowing civic space, and it urged him to prioritize fundamental freedoms and democratic institutions. This is negative evidence against equal treatment of unpopular viewpoints and opposition constituencies.  
  IDs: `4B.7` `4B.3` `4B.5` `4B.6`

- **World Report 2024: Democratic Republic of Congo** | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/democratic-republic-congo)  
  HRW says repression against journalists, activists, government critics, and opposition members continued; police used excessive force against peaceful demonstrators; and authorities targeted opposition party officials. This is strong evidence against political equality for opposition and unpopular viewpoints.  
  IDs: `4B.7` `4B.3` `4B.5` `4B.6`

- **DRC: President Felix Tshisekedi must be held accountable for human rights violations** | Amnesty International | 2024-09-30 | [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/drc-president-felix-tshisekedi-must-be-held-accountable-for-human-rights-violations/)  
  Amnesty said the state of siege concentrated power in military and police officials, militarized daily life, and coincided with a crackdown on dissent. That is direct evidence of coercive treatment of excluded viewpoints, not equal political protection.  
  IDs: `4B.7` `4B.3` `4B.5` `4B.6`

- **DR Congo’s arrest of activists invokes déjà vu of growing repression** | Amnesty International | 2024-02-16 | [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/dr-congos-arrest-of-activists-invokes-deja-vu-of-growing-repression/)  
  Security services arrested LUCHA activists in abduction-like fashion, held some in unknown detention, and used violence and threats. This is direct evidence against equal treatment for civil-society actors and dissenting groups.  
  IDs: `4B.7` `4B.3` `4B.5` `4B.6`

- **DR Congo authorities must immediately free detained journalist** | Amnesty International | 2024-03-08 | [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/drc-authorities-must-immediately-free-detained-journalist/)  
  Amnesty described Stanis Bujakera’s detention as judicial harassment meant to chill criticism. This is strong evidence against protection of unpopular viewpoints and independent criticism.  
  IDs: `4B.7` `4B.3` `4B.5` `4B.6`

- **Congo police break up small protest over parliamentary election results** | Reuters | 2024-01-16 | [URL](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-police-break-up-small-protest-over-parliamentary-election-results-2024-01-16/)  
  Police dispersed a Kinshasa protest, beating some participants and arresting others. This is direct evidence against equal political treatment for opposition-aligned protesters.  
  IDs: `4B.7` `4B.3` `4B.5`

- **DR Congo president draws criticism over constitutional reform plans** | Reuters | 2024-10-24 | [URL](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-president-tshisekedi-draws-criticism-over-constitutional-reform-plans-2024-10-24/)  
  Tshisekedi launched a constitutional review process that raised fears it could remove term limits and clear the way for a third term. That is strong evidence of political entrenchment, not equal contestability or equal treatment of opponents.  
  IDs: `4B.7` `4B.1` `4B.5`

- **DR Congo constitutional court rejects petitions against provisional election results** | Reuters | 2024-01-10 | [URL](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/dr-congo-constitutional-court-rejects-petitions-against-provisional-election-results-2024-01-10/)  
  Reuters noted that opposition figures refused to rely on the court because they did not trust state institutions. This is indirect but relevant evidence that neutral institutions were not experienced as equally accessible or protective for opposition actors.  
  IDs: `4B.7` `4B.4` `4B.5`

- **Congo election commission overspent, awarded opaque contracts-report** | Reuters | 2024-01-15 | [URL](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-election-commission-overspent-awarded-opaque-contracts-report-2024-01-15/)  
  A civil-society report said CENI failed to account for about $400 million and used opaque procurement, with calls for investigation. This is negative evidence for equal, neutral treatment in electoral administration.  
  IDs: `4B.7` `4B.4` `4B.5`

- **World Report 2025: Democratic Republic of Congo** | Human Rights Watch | 2025 | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2025/country-chapters/democratic-republic-congo)  
  HRW says authorities cracked down on opposition members, activists, critics, and journalists throughout 2024, including excessive force against a Kinshasa opposition protest and arrests of critics online and offline. This is the strongest single summary of the 2024 repression pattern.  
  IDs: `4B.7` `4B.3` `4B.5` `4B.6`

- **DRC: Human rights priorities for the government of Democratic Republic of Congo during President Tshisekedi’s second term** | Amnesty International | 2024-06-24 | [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/afr62/8155/2024/en/)  
  Amnesty said there had been little to no progress on earlier human-rights pledges and that the state needed to end the state of siege, stop arbitrary detention, and strengthen rule-of-law protections. This is broad negative evidence that the government had not protected political equality in practice.  
  IDs: `4B.7` `4B.3` `4B.4` `4B.5`

**Search Gap**
I found one strong affirmative signal for women’s inclusion and one limited affirmative signal for communal peace in a conflict region. I did not find evidence that Tshisekedi built a broader, durable equality framework for minorities, excluded groups, opposition regions, or unpopular viewpoints in 2024. The dominant evidence points the other way: repression, intimidation, and unequal access to institutions.
